page: Amazon Web Services m9g.24xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor allocation is fully dedicated with 1.0 thread per core, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 96 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 191594.32 and a PassMark CPU extended instructions test score of 128808.56. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching a top-tier read-only small block speed of 13865.98 GB/sec and a large block read speed of 365.0 GB/sec. The server excels in data processing tasks, demonstrating top-tier performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1089.01 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 266.43 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning workloads, it achieves a top-tier prompt processing speed of 3898.19 tokens per second using a small 135M model, though text generation speeds for the same model drop to an average tier of 91.32 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.24xlarge offers a high-density resource profile, leveraging the ARMv9 architecture to deliver strong multi-threaded performance and memory throughput without the overhead of hyperthreading. The absence of local storage means storage requirements must be handled externally, which represents a tradeoff for data-intensive local operations. This server is highly suited for scale-out workloads, multi-threaded data compression, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and intermediate language model prompt processing.
